feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for a senior digital communications leader: the experience progression is clear, the scope is substantial, and the public-sector specialization comes through well. Writing is polished overall, but the document is somewhat repetitive, light on quantified outcomes beyond traffic/platform scale, and slightly overpacked with overlapping skills sections.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression within NACo, showing increasing leadership, ownership, and technical breadth.  
- Strong credibility through concrete platform scale: 10,000+ pages, 3.5 million annual page views, 50+ internal publishers, and named tools/platforms.  
- Good positioning for digital strategy/web modernization roles, with a compelling mix of governance, analytics, CMS, multimedia, and AI-enabled search.

1. Top improvements  
- Add more outcome-based metrics: show impact on engagement, efficiency, adoption, search performance, campaign results, cost savings, or team productivity—not just responsibilities and platform size.  
- Reduce duplication across “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT”; consolidate to improve scannability and make the CV feel tighter.  
- Minor style/consistency issues: “Coleman DAVIS” capitalization is unusual; punctuation around list items is inconsistent; “social, and multimedia” has an unnecessary comma; “A2/Learning” reads awkwardly; “10×20-foot” may be clearer as “10 x 20-foot.” No obvious misspellings or major grammar errors.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro with clear seniority and sector focus, but it reads broad and repeats themes already covered in the subtitle, competencies, and experience. It would be stronger with one or two concrete scale signals and tighter phrasing.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace generic “building the platforms” language with sharper action verbs and outcomes; e.g., “Leads enterprise web modernization, governance, analytics, and editorial operations for high-volume public-sector communications.”
- Add a concrete scale marker from recent experience to increase impact, such as “10,000+ page website,” “3.5M annual page views,” or “50+ internal publishers.”
- Trim the list slightly to avoid sounding exhaustive; group related items (e.g., “editorial and multimedia operations”).
- Consider revised version: “Digital platform and communications leader with 12+ years of experience modernizing high-volume public-sector web ecosystems. Leads enterprise website transformation, governance, analytics, editorial and multimedia operations, and AI-enabled content discovery for complex, mission-driven organizations.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled user experiences” overlaps with Core Competencies and Recent Projects; “AI-enabled content discovery” would be more specific.
- “Platforms, governance models and content operations” overlaps heavily with the subtitle and competencies section.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and work experience. It would be stronger if tightened to emphasize distinctive leadership-level capabilities rather than repeating broad phrases.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use parallel noun phrases and sharpen wording: “Enterprise web modernization” instead of “Enterprise website modernization.”
- Consider a tighter version: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial operations • Analytics, reporting, and insight infrastructure • Cross-channel communications leadership • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integration • Public-sector advocacy communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations
- Replace “content experiences” with “content discovery” or “user experiences” for clearer meaning.
- Use “and” instead of “&” if the rest of the CV favors a more formal style.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise website modernization,” “analytics infrastructure,” “AI-enabled search,” and “multimedia production” are already stated in the header and repeated in Topline Skills.
- “Advocacy and public-sector communications” overlaps with the subtitle and multiple NACo roles; keep only if you want sector specialization foregrounded.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot, but it reads dense and overlaps heavily with the NACo experience bullets. Tightening phrasing and emphasizing outcomes, scope, or distinct formats would make it feel more additive.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Add a one-line intro such as “Selected recent projects” and keep each item to one crisp, parallel sentence.
- Strengthen specificity: use consistent action verbs and, where possible, add scale or purpose (e.g., “for county officials,” “conference activation,” “Drupal 10 campaign microsite”).
- Improve style consistency: spell out “10-by-20-foot” instead of “10×20-foot,” and use serial commas consistently.
- Consider this tighter version: “Selected recent projects: AI Hybrid Search—Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience using hybrid retrieval, vector search, structured content workflows, and bill-level chat. We Are Counties Microsite—Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, and downloadable resources. Organization Anniversary Campaign—Developed a multi-part digital campaign featuring editorial storytelling, archival media, web features, and a 10-by-20-foot interactive conference display. Advocacy Video Series—Produced a recurring advocacy video program spanning planning, production, and distribution across web, email, and social.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI Hybrid Search, microsites, and advocacy video series all repeat points already covered in Work Experience.
- If space is tight, keep only the most distinctive project formats not already obvious from the experience section.

items.title: Coleman DAVIS
items.subtitle: Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader
items.content: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience building the platforms, governance models and content operations behind high-volume public-sector communications. Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Email

items.title: Website
items.content: https://colemanpdavis.com/

items.title: Core Competencies
items.content: Enterprise website modernization • Digital governance & editorial systems • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Advocacy and public-sector communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant current role, but it reads as a broad service list. Tighten it around highest-value consulting outcomes and distinguish it from the prior NACo staff roles by emphasizing advisory/consulting scope, platform builds, and AI search leadership.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper summary: “Advise NACo on enterprise digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations, and web modernization as an external consultant.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets into 4–5 impact-led bullets; start with strong verbs: “Built,” “Led,” “Designed,” “Advised.”
- Add measurable scope where possible: number of sites/properties supported, campaign launches, toolkit downloads, workflow improvements, search accuracy/engagement gains, or time saved.
- Example rewrite: “Led development of AI-enabled search, defining retrieval strategy, structured content workflows, and discovery UX for complex policy content.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “digital strategy, content operations, governance, workflows” overlaps heavily with the 2022–2024 Director role; keep this entry focused on consulting deliverables completed since Oct. 2024.
- Microsites, AI search, and campaigns also appear in Recent Projects; avoid repeating the same phrasing verbatim.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It will be stronger if you tighten the opening, foreground the biggest outcomes, and avoid repeating channel-management details already covered in adjacent NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the broad first sentence with a sharper scope/outcome line: “Directed NACo’s digital media function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Lead with the website modernization bullet and make it more outcome-driven: “Led redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page Drupal website, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Tighten channel-management language and add performance metrics if available: email open/click growth, social engagement, production volume, cost savings, or turnaround improvements.
- Combine operations/governance/analytics into one concise bullet emphasizing decision-making and efficiency: “Built reporting and governance systems across GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery, improving visibility, publishing consistency, and cross-team planning.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; keep this entry focused on enterprise leadership and transformation.
- Video-program language may duplicate older NACo entries unless framed here as building the in-house studio/capability.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps with both the later Director role and the earlier Digital Media Manager role. Make it more specific to what changed under your ownership at this level, with tighter phrasing and clearer outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + level: “Managed day-to-day digital communications operations across NACo’s web, email, social and video channels, improving editorial coordination and advocacy delivery.”
- Tighten bullets to emphasize ownership: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Reframe video bullet around launch/growth: “Produced and scaled a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Combine workflow/editorial bullets: “Built stronger cross-team editorial planning and publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams, improving consistency and execution.” Add metrics if possible (open rates, production volume, turnaround time, audience growth).

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital communications operations across web, email, social and video” is very similar to the Director role; keep this entry more execution-focused.
- Weekly video updates also appear in the 2015–2018 role; clarify this role as scaling/formalizing the program, not starting it.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this item is too generic and overlaps heavily with the header, Core Competencies, and recent NACo roles. Tighten it to emphasize senior-level leadership areas not already repeated elsewhere.

Suggested edit:
- Replace broad phrases with sharper, executive-level wording:  
- Enterprise digital strategy & governance  
- Editorial operations and publishing standards  
- Cross-channel communications leadership  
- Public-sector advocacy communications  
- Audience-centered content strategy
- Consider swapping “Audience-focused content planning” for “Content governance and editorial planning” if you want stronger alignment with recent leadership scope.
- If space allows, make one line more outcome-oriented, e.g., “Enterprise digital strategy for high-volume public-sector communications.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy,” “editorial systems and governance,” and “multi-channel communications leadership” substantially repeat Core Competencies and the header summary.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” overlaps with “Advocacy and public-sector communications”; keep only one version across sections.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:

- WordPress
- SharePoint

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it reads as a generic tool list and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. This topline item should emphasize higher-value, recent platform leadership and implementation strengths rather than exhaustive technologies.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tool inventory to capability-led phrasing tied to recent work: “Drupal platform leadership • CMS modernization and migration • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) • API and workflow integrations • Airtable-based operational systems • AI-enabled search experiences”
- Remove lower-signal or older items unless central to target roles; consider dropping “WordPress,” “SharePoint,” “Power Pages,” and “jQuery” from this topline line.
- Use “front-end implementation” instead of listing every language here; keep detailed stack in “Technical + IT.”
- If space allows, sharpen impact orientation: “Enterprise Drupal delivery” or “Large-scale CMS modernization” to echo the 10,000+ page migration.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item duplicates much of “Technical + IT”; keep topline skills strategic and save full platform/tool lists for the technical section.
- “AI-enabled search experiences” already appears in Core Competencies; avoid repeating it verbatim in multiple places if space is tight.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster for recent leadership roles, but it reads as a raw tool list and overlaps heavily with “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT. Make it more outcome-oriented and executive-level.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-only to capability + decision impact, e.g. “Analytics strategy, reporting and optimization.”
- Tighten and group items: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI and Microsoft Clarity” rather than separate bullets.
- Replace generic phrases with stronger business language: “KPI framework development” instead of “KPI design”; “executive dashboarding and leadership reporting” instead of “Leadership reporting.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This substantially duplicates “Technical + IT > Data, Analytics & Optimization”; keep Topline Skills higher-level and leave the full tool inventory there.
- “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” already appears in Core Competencies, so avoid repeating that exact phrase verbatim.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill area, but this item is too generic and overlaps heavily with the Core Competencies line and multiple NACo roles. Make it more senior, operational, and distinctive rather than listing basic production tasks.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to something broader and more leadership-level, e.g. **Multimedia Operations & Event Production**

- Broadcast-quality video production and post-production
- Livestream and hybrid event production
- In-house studio buildout and operations
- PTZ camera and multi-camera production workflows
- Virtual event and advocacy content delivery
- If space allows, emphasize scale or ownership rather than tools alone, e.g. “studio operations” → “broadcast studio operations”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Livestreaming” and “multimedia production” already appear in Core Competencies; avoid repeating the same wording.
- This section should not restate older hands-on duties too heavily, since recent roles position you more as the leader who built and ran the function.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it reads as a generic inventory and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. This item should either add specificity or be trimmed to avoid repetition.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe to emphasize depth and recency: “Drupal (enterprise migrations, modular content architecture) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages”
- If space allows, add proficiency cues tied to recent work: “Drupal 9/10” or “Drupal (10,000+ page migration; 50+ publishers)” to reinforce impact.
- Consider dropping GitHub Pages unless it supports a meaningful project; it feels lighter than the rest of the stack.
- Keep naming consistent with the rest of the CV: use either “CMS platforms” or “Web Platforms & CMS” across sections.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates Topline Skills [2]; consider removing one version or making this section more technical/specific.
- Drupal is already strongly evidenced in recent roles and projects, so avoid repeating it elsewhere without added context.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical coverage, but this reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Tighten it to emphasize implementation depth and modern tools most relevant to recent work.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: **Front-end & Technical Implementation:** HTML5/CSS3 • JavaScript/jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
- Consider dropping version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) unless other skills also use versioning; “HTML/CSS” is cleaner and more current.
- If accurate, add one higher-value qualifier instead of more tools, e.g., “custom Drupal front-end implementation,” “deployment automation,” or “serverless scripting” to show applied use.
- Order by strength/relevance: JavaScript • API integrations • GTM • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions • HTML/CSS

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills.
- “GitHub Actions” may overlap with “Workflow automation”; keep it here only if you want this section to signal hands-on technical execution.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item is too broad and mixes automation platforms with project/collaboration tools. It also overlaps with “Workflow automation,” “Airtable systems,” and cross-functional planning already emphasized in recent roles.

Suggested edit:
- Split by function and tighten wording: “Automation & Workflow: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier” and move Jira/Asana/Basecamp/Trello to a separate “Project & Work Management” line.
- Remove Slack and Teams from this item unless collaboration tools are listed consistently elsewhere; they dilute the automation focus.
- Consider a more impact-oriented label: “Workflow Automation & Work Management.”
- If accurate, add scope qualifiers in a summary section instead of here, e.g., “built cross-team workflow systems in Airtable/Power Automate” or “supported editorial planning across 50+ publishers.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already appear in Core Competencies and Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same emphasis here without added specificity.
- Jira/Asana/Basecamp/Trello echo planning/governance themes already covered in recent NACo roles.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This is relevant to the candidate’s recent leadership in email operations, but it reads as a generic tool list. Strengthen it by signaling enterprise-scale email/engagement capability and aligning terminology with the rest of the CV.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms**
- Rewrite as: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, add scope-oriented wording elsewhere in this section or adjacent skills, e.g. **enterprise email automation**, **newsletter operations**, or **member engagement platforms**
- Use the most current product naming consistently: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys** rather than a slash format

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps with work experience bullets about leading email newsletters reaching tens of thousands; avoid repeating audience scale here unless you add a distinct systems/automation angle.
- “Multi-channel communications operations” already appears in Core Competencies, so keep this item tool-focused rather than strategic.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools list, but it overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills” and misses a chance to show level or business use. Tighten it into a more technical stack line and avoid generic terms.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: “GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • BigQuery • Looker Studio • Power BI • SEO analysis • Experimentation (A/B testing) • Executive dashboarding”
- Replace generic nouns with clearer capability labels: “SEO” → “SEO analysis”; “Dashboarding” → “Executive dashboarding” or “KPI reporting.”
- If space allows, add one qualifier tied to recent impact, e.g., “analytics stack for 10,000+ page site” or “reporting for 3.5M annual page views.”
- Keep the order by strategic weight/recent use: GA4, Clarity, BigQuery, BI/reporting tools, then optimization skills.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially duplicates “Topline Skills > Analytics, Insights & Optimization.” Consider deleting one section or making this version more tool-only while leaving outcomes/capabilities in Topline Skills.
- “A/B testing” is not evidenced elsewhere; keep only if you can support it in experience bullets.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is too general and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more foundational and execution-focused, with clearer scope and any metrics you can add.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize early-team building and hands-on delivery: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team, supporting web, email, social and multimedia operations.”
- Add concrete outputs/results if available: website refresh scope, livestream/event volume, video cadence, audience growth, email/social performance, or process improvements.
- Tighten the second sentence: “Supported a major website refresh, produced recurring livestreams and weekly video updates, and improved day-to-day publishing workflows.”
- Clarify supervision modestly: replace “providing day-to-day guidance” with “mentored a digital media associate on production and publishing workflows.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “weekly video updates” and workflow improvement overlap with the 2018–2022 role; frame this entry as the launch/foundation stage.
- Avoid broad channel lists if no outcomes are added; later roles already cover enterprise oversight.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry, but it reads generic and overlaps with later NACo roles in digital/media. Emphasize the podcast launch as the clearest differentiator and tighten the research/program support language.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground the unique achievement: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy priorities, while contributing digital and multimedia content.”
- Make the second sentence stronger and more concise: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting and production.”
- If accurate, add scope or outcome: number of episodes, audience, internal adoption, or how the podcast supported advocacy/member engagement.
- Consider replacing “contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials” with a more specific verb/result, e.g., “produced multimedia assets for program and policy communications.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid broad “digital content production” phrasing that repeats later digital/media roles.
- Don’t overstate team leadership here; later entries already show progression into management.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is relevant, but it currently mixes software with capabilities and repeats multimedia themes already covered in Core Competencies and Topline Skills. Make it tighter and more tool-focused, with only the most distinctive production capabilities retained.

Suggested edit
- Rename or tighten to emphasize tools first: “Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Podcast production • Livestream studio operations”
- Replace “Livestream studio workflows” with “Livestream studio operations” for stronger, cleaner phrasing that aligns with your studio-building leadership.
- If space allows elsewhere, separate tools from capabilities: software here; production capabilities in “Multimedia Production & Event Delivery.”
- Only keep “Podcast production” if you want to preserve that distinct early-career credential; otherwise cut it for concision.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Livestream studio workflows” overlaps with “Multimedia production and livestream operations,” “Livestreaming,” and “Studio operations.”
- This section should avoid repeating broad production skills already demonstrated in recent NACo roles.
